  "book_id": "6993899a0f04c37dcfa61b3c",
  "slot": 5,
  "title": "Sophocles, Hesiod, Euripides (18 tragedies), and Aeschylus",
  "tradition": "greek-latin-classics",
  "shelf_fit": "fits",
  "shelf_note": "A 14th-century manuscript containing works of major Greek tragedians and Hesiod perfectly matches the greek-latin-classics tradition.",
  "rights_flag": null,
  "structure_note": "The high number of printed repeats (143) and backsteps (33) likely reflects misread manuscript foliation numbers rather than actual structural defects. There is also a small discrepancy between pages with OCR (507) and pages translated (503).",
  "on_sight_defect": true,
  "fit_to_show": "do_not_show",
  "showcase_pages": [],
  "reader_summary": "A reader of this tradition will find a 14th-century manuscript containing classical Greek tragedies and poetry. However, the Greek transcription is severely corrupted by hallucinations that replace the actual text, as well as rampant XML tag leakage. Consequently, the English translation reflects these errors and missing passages, making the text completely untrustworthy.",
  "book_verdict": "The pipeline fails on this manuscript, with the transcription model hallucinating Greek text, dropping passages, and leaking XML tags and English image descriptions into the reader pane. These severe errors cascade into the translation, rendering the book unreadable."
}

{
  "book_id": "69a5e60885fa13e734e42186",
  "slot": 6,
  "title": "Procli In Platonis Alcibiadem Commentarius (Barocci 140)",
  "tradition": "greek-latin-classics",
  "shelf_fit": "fits",
  "shelf_note": "The book is a Greek manuscript of a philosophical commentary, which correctly belongs in the classics tradition.",
  "rights_flag": null,
  "structure_note": "The backsteps and repeats in the printed page counts are likely due to OCR misreadings of manuscript foliation.",
  "on_sight_defect": true,
  "fit_to_show": "do_not_show",
  "showcase_pages": [],
  "reader_summary": "The reader will find the correct Greek manuscript of Proclus' Commentary on Plato's Alcibiades. However, the transcription is fundamentally broken by hallucinated XML tags and severe misreadings that alter the philosophical meaning. The English translation cannot be trusted because it routinely incorporates the transcription's errors and translates the fabricated tags.",
  "book_verdict": "The text is severely defective on sight due to rampant XML tag leakage and serious OCR misreadings that corrupt the text's meaning. The translation compounds these issues by attempting to translate the OCR hallucinations, rendering the book unusable."
}

{
  "book_id": "69a9768ee12635ded71c4e2f",
  "slot": 7,
  "title": "Quaestiones de Primis Principiis",
  "tradition": "greek-latin-classics",
  "shelf_fit": "fits",
  "shelf_note": "This 1826 edition of Damascius is a classical text that correctly belongs in the greek-latin-classics tradition.",
  "rights_flag": null,
  "structure_note": "The 14 printed backsteps and 10 repeats likely result from misread leaf numerals or transitions in front-matter pagination, rather than structural splices, as there are no duplicate records.",
  "on_sight_defect": true,
  "fit_to_show": "do_not_show",
  "showcase_pages": [],
  "reader_summary": "This is an 1826 edition of a philosophical work by Damascius. The transcription captures the right text but is cluttered with leaked structural XML tags and invented vocabulary lists. The English translation cannot be trusted because it systematically drops footnotes, critical apparatus, and occasionally entire clauses from the source.",
  "book_verdict": "The reading experience is severely compromised by raw markup tags leaking into the text. The translation is unacceptable for scholarly use due to its frequent omission of critical apparatus and main text."
}

{
  "book_id": "69b52c953dd6d94230281474",
  "slot": 8,
  "title": "Vitruvii de architectura libri X",
  "tradition": "greek-latin-classics",
  "shelf_fit": "fits",
  "shelf_note": "A 13th-century Latin manuscript of Vitruvius fits the Greek and Latin classics tradition.",
  "rights_flag": null,
  "structure_note": "The 18 printed backsteps and 14 repeats out of 116 pages likely reflect misread folio numerals or unnumbered versos typical of manuscript foliation.",
  "on_sight_defect": true,
  "fit_to_show": "do_not_show",
  "showcase_pages": [],
  "reader_summary": "This is a scan of a 13th-century Latin manuscript of Vitruvius. The transcription is heavily polluted with leaked XML tags, English image descriptions, and model reasoning masquerading as text. The English translation is untrustworthy, dropping large sections, hallucinating sentences from garbled OCR, and substituting Arabic flyleaf text with invented editorial notes.",
  "book_verdict": "While the manuscript fits the collection, the extraction pipeline has failed catastrophically on it. Rampant XML tag leakage, model reasoning printed as source text, and highly defective translations render the presentation unusable."
}
